comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C6 regarding agrinC two-layer organization. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with high confidence. Reviewers praised the 'very high quality' data and 'robust morphometric measurements,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of converging evidence from multiple imaging modalities.

Complete agreement on claims C7-C11 regarding agrin orientation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers' general praise for 'novel insights into the organization of ECM' implicitly supports these structural claims, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of strong quantitative and biochemical evidence.

Agreement on claims C12-C13 regarding integrin β1 localization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns and praised the robust morphometric measurements, aligning with OpenEval's positive assessment of the quantitative STORM data.

Agreement on claims C14-C17 regarding laminin N-terminal domain localization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C66 while peer review includes C18-C19, showing slight differences in claim grouping but consistent positive assessment of the laminin localization findings.

Significant disagreement on claims C20-C23 regarding two separate laminin networks. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with strong validation, but peer reviewer 8 rates this UNCERTAIN, specifically challenging that the two-network interpretation 'depends on data derived from the ectopic expression of human Laminin α5' and requesting refinement of the interpretation.

General agreement on collagen IV localization (C28, C32-C34). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer 7 requested clarification on why periN localization counts are higher than NC1, indicating a minor methodological question rather than challenging the core findings that OpenEval assessed positively.

Partial overlap on collagen IV claims. OpenEval R7 addresses C29-C34 regarding collagen IV isoform distributions (SUPPORTED), while peer R6 addresses C28, C32-C34 (SUPPORTED). Both positive but OpenEval includes additional claims about developmental context and isoform-specific distributions.

Agreement on claim C36 regarding nidogen localization. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted this finding as fitting the overall GBM organization model, consistent with OpenEval's assessment that the data support a cross-linking function.

Disagreement on human GBM findings (C37-C45). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with comprehensive STORM analysis, but peer reviewer 9 rates this UNCERTAIN, noting a critical discrepancy where 'AgrinC is much richer on the podocyte face and almost absent from the capillary side' that was not mentioned by authors, requiring clarification.

Agreement on Alport model findings (C46-C51 in OpenEval, C48-C51 in peer review). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers did not challenge these disease-relevant observations, consistent with OpenEval's positive assessment of the STORM data showing disrupted organization.

Strong agreement on summary conclusions (C69-C73 in OpenEval, C69-C71 in peer review). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly stated the study shows 'ECM in these cells is much more organized than generally believed,' directly aligning with OpenEval's assessment of the integrated conclusions.

OpenEval finds claims C74-C75 regarding laminin orientation models SUPPORTED as reasonable speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these geometric constraint interpretations, though they relate to the overall structural model.

Agreement on functional implications (C76-C78). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted these interpretations about ligand-receptor interactions as part of the study's interest to nephrologists and basement membrane researchers, consistent with OpenEval's positive assessment.

OpenEval rates claims C79-C83 regarding molecular mechanisms and Alport pathogenesis as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic hypotheses, though peer R9 addresses related Alport findings.

Divergence on methodological claims (C84-C85). OpenEval finds the Tokuyasu method selection and technical characterization SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting validation using different fixation methods and clarification on why other super-resolution methods are unsuitable, noting measurements are relative rather than absolute.

OpenEval finds claims C52-C63, C67 regarding established background knowledge SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background/context claims, as they represent cited literature rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

Peer reviewer 2 raised extensive UNCERTAIN concerns about methodological clarity (claims C2, C3, C7, C12, C14, C15, C18, C28, C32, C36, C38), requesting clarification of analysis geometry, region selection, localization definitions, and threshold settings. OpenEval did not identify these methodological reporting issues as a separate evaluation, instead assessing the scientific claims themselves as supported.
